classification.difficultyReason: Extend the supplied acute-proof technique to the obtuse/reflex configuration, using the specified diameter scaffold and cyclic supplementary angles before a separate reflex-centre proof.

content.prompt:
Show that the alternate segment theorem holds when the angle between the tangent and the chord is obtuse.

Let $\angle P=\alpha$. We must prove $\angle SAB=\alpha$.

spec.description: Obtuse tangent–chord proof with constructed diameter AN and chord NB.
spec.mathematics: N is antipodal A; P is on minor arc AB, so APB is obtuse; AS and AT are true tangent rays.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens, named points and unknowns; no calculated answers.

sizing.exceptionReason: Circle/tangent incidences and complete10pt labels determine the required width; final height and label clearance require the existing rendered review.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Construct diameter $AN$ and chord $NB$. Show that $\angle ANB=180^\circ-\alpha$.

answer.worked:
$A,N,B,P$ lie on the circle. Opposite angles of cyclic quadrilateral $ANBP$ are supplementary, so
$$\angle ANB+\angle APB=180^\circ.$$
Since $\angle APB=\alpha$, $\angle ANB=180^\circ-\alpha$.

$AN$ is a diameter, so $\angle ABN=90^\circ$ (angle in a semicircle). In $\triangle ABN$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle NAB&=180^\circ-\angle ABN-\angle ANB\\&=180^\circ-90^\circ-(180^\circ-\alpha)\\&=\alpha-90^\circ.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Using $\angle SAB=\angle SAN+\angle NAB$, show that $\angle SAB=\alpha$.

answer.worked:
$SA\perp AN$ (tangent and radius at $A$), so $\angle SAN=90^\circ$. Therefore
$$\angle SAB=90^\circ+(\alpha-90^\circ)=\alpha.$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Use the technique used in question 4 to prove the alternate segment theorem for an obtuse angle.

answer.worked:
Join $OA$ and $OB$. The reflex angle $AOB$ standing on the same major arc $AB$ as $\angle APB$ is $2\alpha$. Thus the minor angle $AOB$ is $360^\circ-2\alpha$.

Since $OA=OB$,
$$\angle OAB=\frac{180^\circ-(360^\circ-2\alpha)}2=\alpha-90^\circ.$$

Also, $\angle SAO=90^\circ$ (radius and tangent). Therefore
$$\angle SAB=\angle SAO+\angle OAB=90^\circ+(\alpha-90^\circ)=\alpha.$$
